Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. Nathaniel Hlabangana and Kupakwashe Muradzi to open for Zimbabwe Under-19. Al Fahad to bowl first. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Late Firepower from the Bangla middle-order - Bangladesh was 80 for 3 in the 21st over, but a crucial partnership between Azizul and Rizan helped stabilize the innings by adding 73 runs to the total. The Bangladeshi skipper eventually fell to Tatenda after playing a solid knock of 58 runs from 87 balls. Following his departure, a strong partnership developed, but the lower middle order contributed enough runs to set a target of 253 runs. Especially it was Md Abdullah's and Iqbal Hossain's quick fire in the last two overs that made the difference in the score. The question now looms that, is this total sufficient for the Chevron batters? We'll have to wait to find out. Stay tuned as we will be back shorter for the chase!

Shelton Mazvitorera is up for a chat - Mazvitorera commends the team's effort in the field, particularly with bowling and fielding. Although they didn't expect the opposition to reach 250, he acknowledges the team's good effort. He believes that if the team fields well and applies pressure on the batters with the ball, the wickets will follow. He thinks the target is gettable and is confident that if his team bats out their overs, they can certainly chase down the score.

The crucial 4th wicket partnership - Bangladesh displayed a cautious approach to their innings, clearly showing no rush to accumulate runs. The openers set the tone by playing with composure, opting for timing over aggressive hitting unless offered a loose delivery. Despite the slow start, Panashe Mazai managed to score the first run for the Chevrons. Following the dismissal of the first wicket, Zawad Abrar and captain Azizul Hakim established a solid partnership. However, a miscommunication during a run attempt led to the end of their 46-run collaboration, allowing Michael Blignaut to seize the opportunity and secure another wicket for his team.

The Bangla skipper led the charge - Bangladesh have posted a total of 253 runs and their skipper has been their star batter from the first inning. For Zimbabwea their fielding has been just up to mark and the bowlers bowled really well throughout the inning, but in the last three overs they gave away 39 runs, and also they could have done a lot better with the extras.

Pitch Report - The players will require their shades today as it's hot and humid out there. The pitch has a bit of moisture due to the heat around. It's rock hard, and the batters should enjoy the conditions.

Zimbabwe Under-19's skipper - Simbarashe Mudzengerere says they were looking to bowl first. Feels in the morning, there might be some movement for the bowlers. Shares the boys need to lock in and keep believing. Hopes the fans will come in numbers today and he promises to give them a good game.

The captain of Bangladesh Under-19 - Azizul Hakim Tamim says they will bat first due to the conditions. Tells that the wicket is good to bat on, so they are happy to bat first. Mentions that this tournament is a good lesson for them. Hopes to end the tournament well.

Expectations for the dead rubber - Although this is a dead rubber in terms of qualification, expect both sides to play with freedom and aggression as they look to avoid finishing at the very bottom of the Super Sixes table. Bangladesh will rely on the technical skill of their top order and the bowling of Sheikh Parvez Jibon, who has taken 11 wickets in the tournament. Conversely, Zimbabwe will look to exploit their home conditions in Harare to pressure the young Tigers early. With nothing to lose, this match offers a platform for individual stars to make a final statement on the world stage before the tournament moves into the knockout phase. Toss and team new in a bit.

Zimbabwe Under-19's hard-fought road - For the co-hosts, Zimbabwe, the tournament has been a steep learning curve against top-tier opposition. Despite spirited performances and local support, they enter this final match frustrated after a massive 204-run defeat to India, where they were bowled out for just 148 while chasing 353. Earlier in the tournament, they also suffered a heavy 8-wicket loss to Pakistan. Leeroy Chiwaula has been the beacon of hope for the home side, tallying some runs so far, while Panashe Mazai leads their bowling attack. For the young Chevrons, this match represents a final chance to reward their home fans with a victory before their home World Cup ends.

Bangladesh Under-19's inconsistent campaign - Bangladesh's journey in the 2026 edition has been a rollercoaster of missed opportunities and weather-interrupted play. Their campaign began with a narrow 18-run loss to India via the DLS method, followed by a frustrating No Result against New Zealand due to rain. Although they showed flashes of brilliance with a dominant 7-wicket victory over the USA to secure their Super Six spot, they were thoroughly outclassed by England in their opening Super 6 fixture, losing by 7 wickets with over 25 overs to spare. Captain Azizul Hakim Tamim has been the standout performer, leading the side with the bat, but he has lacked consistent support from the rest of the batting order. Bowling has done decent but the batting is where they lack the most and will need to improve if they are to get a result in their favor.

Welcome to the Super 6 finale at Harare - Welcome, cricket fans, to the final Super 6 Group 2 fixture for these two nations at the Harare Sports Club. While the atmosphere in the capital remains electric, the stakes for this Match 11 encounter are purely about pride. Both Bangladesh Under-19 and tournament co-hosts Zimbabwe Under-19 have been officially eliminated from semi-final contention following a string of difficult results against the group's heavyweights. Currently, Bangladesh sits in 4th place with a single point from a rain-affected draw, while Zimbabwe occupies the bottom of the table with zero points.
